latest_release.name: RubyLLM 2.2.0
latest_release.body:
RubyLLM 2.2.0 lets a model run the code it writes in a sandbox on your own servers, teaches it your workflows with skills, keeps files and long tool results out of the conversation, and makes persisted chats safe to run from several processes at once. Four more providers join, bringing the built-in total to twenty-three.

```sh
bundle add ruby_llm --version 2.2.0
```

**Upgrading from 2.1?** Require 2.2 in your `Gemfile`, run `bin/rails generate ruby_llm:upgrade`, and run the migration before deploying. 2.2 removes and renames some names, listed under [Changed in 2.2](#changed-in-22), and the [upgrade guide](https://rubyllm.com/upgrading/) gives the exact replacement for each. Applications on 2.0 upgrade to 2.1 first. See [What's New in 2.2](https://rubyllm.com/whats-new-in-2-2/) for examples.

## New

- **Let a model run code on your own servers.** `with_code_execution` gives the model one tool that runs Ruby, Python, JavaScript, or shell in a sandbox built on the [mxc](https://crmne.github.io/mxc/) gem, using Bubblewrap on Linux and Seatbelt on macOS. It needs mxc 0.4.1 or later, so run `bundle update mxc` if you already use it. Files the code writes come back as attachments, and runs emit an event, write a usage row, and report their progress. By @crmne, @stephankaag, and @yorzi. ([93f582e0](https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/commit/93f582e0), [5209fa51](https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/commit/5209fa51), #1227, #1233, #1285, #1487, #1552, #1596)
- **Widen a sandbox one call at a time.** `escalate_to:` lets the model ask for a named sandbox for a single call, with a reason. The call waits for approval like any other, and nothing is remembered for the next one. By @crmne. ([797814b4](https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/commit/797814b4))
- **Teach the model your workflows with skills.** `with_skills` loads folders in the open Agent Skills format only when a task needs them, and their scripts run in the sandbox. The `skill` gem finds and installs them, with `gem exec skill add`, and installs RubyLLM's own skill for your coding assistant. By @crmne and @yorzi. ([8e0b1470](https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/commit/8e0b1470), #1226, #1232, #1235, #1237)
- **Keep files and long tool results out of the conversation.** `with_file_store` keeps them in memory, a folder, or Active Storage, and the model works with them through tools shaped like a coding agent's. Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files need no setup. By @crmne. (#1238, #1443, #1462, #1464, #1469, #1571)
- **Run each persisted chat in one process at a time.** `complete` and the other loop verbs claim the chat first, so a double-submitted approval no longer runs a tool twice. A process that dies gives up its claims within a minute, `Chat.interrupted` finds the chats it left, and the chat UI generator resumes them. A tool call that had started never runs again by itself. By @crmne. ([bf1ff089](https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/commit/bf1ff089), #1517, #1572, #1583, #1586, #1589)
- **Queue messages while a chat runs.** `queue` holds a message until the loop can take it, from any thread or process. A message joins the running turn, or the next one with `steer: false`, and can be withdrawn until it does. By @crmne. (#1223, #1417, #1442, #1534)
- **Let a tool ask the person who runs the chat.** `ask` in a tool pauses the call with no process waiting, and `execute` runs again with the answer. Approvals and MCP server questions share the same `pending_questions` list, and any tool can pause on a long-running task. By @crmne. (#1249, #1257, #1540, #1546)
- **Control the agent loop.** `with_tool_options(rounds:)` stops a model that loops on its tools by raising `RubyLLM::ToolRoundLimitError`, with every call answered. Context budgets keep tool results within the model's window, `exclusive` tools run alone in a round, `around_tool_call` wraps each tool in your block, and `halt` ends the turn from a tool. An agent class now goes wherever tools go, as a subagent. By @crmne. (#1453, #1457, #146

detail.readme:
The Ruby AI framework

Build AI features the Ruby way: models, tools, agents, evaluations, and Rails conventions, designed together, with one consistent API.

```ruby chat = RubyLLM.chat chat.ask "What's the best way to learn Ruby?" chat.ask "What's in this image?", with: "ruby_conf.jpg" chat.with_model("claude-sonnet-5").ask "Now say it as a haiku" RubyLLM.paint("a sunset over mountains in watercolor").save("sunset.png") ```
[Website](https://rubyllm.com/) · [Getting Started](https://rubyllm.com/getting-started/) · [What's New in 2.2](https://rubyllm.com/whats-new-in-2-2/) Battle tested at [](https://chatwithwork.com) - *Fully private work AI* [![Gem Version](https://badge.fury.io/rb/ruby_llm.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/rb/ruby_llm) [![Ruby Style Guide](https://img.shields.io/badge/code_style-rubocop-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop) [![Gem Downloads](https://img.shields.io/gem/dt/ruby_llm)](https://rubygems.org/gems/ruby_llm) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/crmne/ruby_llm/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/crmne/ruby_llm)
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/519fcb20-ab8c-4af3-9185-0953b3ba7b81 > [!NOTE] > Using RubyLLM? [Share your story](https://tally.so/r/3Na02p)! Takes 5 minutes. --- ## 23 providers. One API. Build with the models you want. Move between hosted and local providers without rewriting your application, or connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. [Browse models and pricing](https://rubyllm.com/available-models/) · [Connect a provider](https://rubyllm.com/configuration-providers/) ## A complete AI framework for Ruby More than a client for model APIs. RubyLLM gives your application the conventions, the runtime, and every piece in between, designed to work together. Everything below ships in RubyLLM 2.2. ### Conversations * **Chat:** Conversational AI with `RubyLLM.chat` * **Streaming:** Real-time responses with blocks * **Attachments:** Ask about images, videos, audio, PDFs, and other documents with `with:` * **Structured output:** Define a Ruby schema and read the result with `response.parsed` * **Extended thinking:** Control, view, and persist model deliberation * **Citations:** Normalized source citations from documents, search, and grounding * **Prompt caching:** Turn on the provider's cache with `with_caching` and `cache_until_here` * **Compaction:** Let providers condense long conversations with `with_compaction` * **Token counting:** Count a request before you send it with `count_tokens` * **Fallbacks and cancellation:** Retry on backup models with `with_fallbacks`, stop a run with `cancel` ### Tools and agents * **Tools:** Let AI call your Ruby methods * **Tool approval:** Park a run until a human approves with `requires_approval` * **Provider tools:** Web search, code execution, and MCP connectors with `with_provider_tools` * **MCP:** Connect agents to your systems with server classes in `app/mcp`, per-user inputs, tool filtering, and OAuth with [`RubyLLM::MCP`](https://rubyllm.com/mcp/) * **Agents:** Reusable assistants with `RubyLLM::Agent` * **The agentic loop:** Drive it yourself with `ask_later`, `step`, and `complete?` * **Prompt templates:** ERB prompts in `app/prompts`, rendered with `RubyLLM.render_prompt` * **Workflows:** Correlate multi-agent runs in your telemetry with `RubyLLM.workflow` * **Evaluations:** Reusable datasets, model criteria, and Ruby assertions with [`RubyLLM::Evaluation`](https://rubyllm.com/evaluations/) * **Judgments:** Probabilities, choices, and scores with `RubyLLM::Judge` and `RubyLLM.judge` ### Individual operations * **Image generation:** Create images with `RubyLLM.paint` * **Video generation:** Create videos with `RubyLLM.animate` * **Audio:** Transcribe speech with `RubyLLM.transcribe` and generate it with `RubyLLM.speak` * **OCR:** Turn documents into markdown with `RubyLLM.ocr` * **Embeddings:** Generate embeddings with `RubyLLM.embed` * **Reranking:** Order retrieval candidates by relevance with `RubyLLM.rerank` * **Moderation:** Content flags, categories, and scores with `RubyLLM.moderate` * **Files:** Upload once and reuse across chats with `RubyLLM.upload` * **Batches:** Provider-side batch processing with provider-specific discounts via `RubyLLM.batch` ### Rails and production * **Rails:** Active Record persistence, Active Storage attachments, Hotwire streaming, and generators * **Cost tracking:** A per-attempt usage ledger behind `chat.tokens` and `chat.cost` * **Observability:** Instrumentation events and OpenTelemetry tracing * **Async:** Fiber-based concurrency * **Model registry:** Browse capabilities, limits, and pricing across providers * **Providers:** OpenAI, Azure, xAI, Anthropic, Gemini, VertexAI, Bedrock, Cohere, DeepSeek, Hetzner, Meta, MiniMax, Mistral, Moonshot AI, Ollama, Ollama Cloud, OpenRouter, Perplexity, GPUStack, ElevenLabs, Deepgram, TypeSafe, Z.ai, and any OpenAI-compatible API ### New in 2.2 * **Code execution:** Let the model run Ruby, Python, JavaScript, and shell in a sandbox on your servers with [`with_code_execution`](https://rubyllm.com/code-execution/) * **Skills:** Teach the model your workflows with folders of instructions and scripts in the Agent Skills format with [`with_skills`](https://rubyllm.com/skills/) * **File stores:** Keep attachments and long tool results out of the conversation with [`with_file_store`](https://rubyllm.com/file-stores/) * **Message queueing:** Add messages while a chat runs with `queue` * **More providers:** Meta, MiniMax, Moonshot AI, and Z.ai ## Evaluate your agents Keep questions and expected answers in a dataset. RubyLLM checks correctness by default. Run the same evaluation from Ruby, RSpec, Minitest, or Rake. `app/agents/support_agent.rb` ```ruby class SupportAgent < RubyLLM::Agent instructions "Accept returns of unopened items within 30 days." end ``` `app/evals/support_evaluation.rb` ```ruby class SupportEvaluation < RubyLLM::Evaluation def perform(input) SupportAgent.new.ask(input) end end ``` `app/evals/support_evaluation.yml` ```yaml cases: - name: within_return_window inputs: Can I return an unopened item after 14 days? expected_output: Yes, unopened items can be returned within 30 days. - name: past_return_window inputs: Can I return an unopened item after 45 days? expected_output: No, the 30-day return window has passed. ``` Run the evaluation: ```ruby report = SupportEvaluation.run report.passed? report.cost.total ``` The model evaluator checks meaning, so answers can use different wording. Declare your own criteria, add Ruby assertions, or choose a configured evaluator agent or judgment model. [Read the evaluation guides](https://rubyllm.com/evaluations/). ## Feels at home in Rails Save conversations with Active Record and stream replies with Hotwire. The generators give you a working chat UI. Watch the two-minute demo. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65422091-9338-47da-a303-92b918bd1345 ```bash # Install Rails Integration bin/rails generate ruby_llm:install bin/rails db:migrate bin/rails ruby_llm:load_models # Add Chat UI (optional) bin/rails generate ruby_llm:chat_ui ``` ```ruby class Chat < ApplicationRecord acts_as_chat end chat = Chat.create! model: "gpt-6-luna" chat.ask "What's in this file?", with: "report.pdf" ``` Start your Rails server and visit `http://localhost:3000/chats` to try the chat interface. See the [Rails guide](https://rubyllm.com/rails/) for persistence, streaming, and background jobs. ## Start with one line. Add files, tools, and agents These examples use **2.2.0**. Follow [Getting Started](https://rubyllm.com/getting-started/) to install it and configure the providers you want to try. For 1.x, use the [1.x docs](https://rubyllm.com/v1/). ```ruby # Just ask RubyLLM.chat.ask "What's the best way to learn Ruby?" ``` ```ruby # Ask about files with a model that supports their input types chat = RubyLLM.chat(model: "gemini-3.7-flash") chat.ask "What's in this image?", with: "ruby_conf.jpg" chat.ask "What's happening in this video?", with: "video.mp4" chat.ask "Describe this meeting", with: "meeting.wav" chat.ask "Summarize this document", with: "contract.pdf" chat.ask "Explain this code", with: "app.rb" ``` ```ruby # Multiple files at once chat.ask "Analyze these files", with: ["diagram.png", "report.pdf", "notes.txt"] ``` ```ruby # Stream responses chat.ask "Tell me a story about Ruby" do |chunk| print chunk.content end ``` ```ruby # Generate images image = RubyLLM.paint "a sunset over mountains in watercolor style" image.save "sunset.png" ``` ```ruby # Generate videos video = RubyLLM.animate "a paper boat sailing down a rainy gutter" video.save "paper_boat.mp4" ``` ```ruby # Create embeddings embedding = RubyLLM.embed "Ruby is elegant and expressive" embedding.vector ``` ```ruby # Rank search results documents = ["Reset your password in Settings.", "Invoices arrive by email."] ranked = RubyLLM.rerank("How do I reset my password?", documents, model: "rerank-v3.5") ranked.results.first.document ``` ```ruby # Transcribe audio to text transcript = RubyLLM.transcribe "meeting.wav" puts transcript.text ``` ```ruby # Turn text into speech speech = RubyLLM.speak "Hello, welcome to RubyLLM!" speech.save "welcome.mp3" ``` ```ruby # Extract document text as markdown document = RubyLLM.ocr "contract.pdf" puts document.markdown ``` ```ruby # Check whether a moderation model flags content RubyLLM.moderate("Some user-generated content").flagged? ``` ```ruby # Ask a typed question about your data class Urgency < RubyLLM::Judge probability :urgent, "Does this need attention today?" end Urgency.judge("Please refund my duplicate charge today.").urgent.probability ``` ```ruby # Let AI use your code class Weather < RubyLLM::Tool description "Get current weather" def execute(latitude:, longitude:) url = "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=#{latitude}&longitude=#{longitude}¤t=temperature_2m,wind_speed_10m" JSON.parse(Faraday.get(url).body) end end chat.with_tools(Weather).ask "What's the weather in Berlin?" ``` ```ruby # Define an agent with instructions + tools class WeatherAssistant < RubyLLM::Agent model "gpt-6-luna" instructions "Be concise and always use tools for weather." tools Weather end WeatherAssistant.new.ask "What's the weather in Berlin?" ``` ```ruby # Get structured output class ProductSchema < Schematist::Schema string :name number :price array :features do string end end response = chat.with_schema(ProductSchema).ask "Analyze this product", with: "product.txt" response.parsed ``` ## Installation Install RubyLLM 2.2: ```bash bundle add ruby_llm --version 2.2.0 ``` Configure a provider in your script, or in `config/initializers/ruby_llm.rb` in Rails: ```ruby require 'ruby_llm' RubyLLM.configure do |config| config.openai_api_key = ENV.fetch('OPENAI_API_KEY') end ``` Configure the other providers used by the examples as needed: Gemini for files, xAI for video, Mistral for OCR, and Cohere for reranking. [Getting Started](https://rubyllm.com/getting-started/) shows each setup beside its example. Upgrading an existing app? Follow the [upgrade guide](https://rubyllm.com/upgrading/). Coming from ruby-openai or langchainrb? Follow the [ruby-openai migration guide](https://rubyllm.com/migrate/ruby-openai/), or see [every migration and comparison guide](https://rubyllm.com/migrating-from/). ## AI coding assistants Give your coding assistant the RubyLLM API and documentation that match your application. From your application directory, install the skill packaged with your gem: ```bash gem exec skill add "$(bundle show ruby_llm)" --skill rubyllm --agents coding ``` `--agents coding` installs it for the coding assistants your project uses, not into your app's `app/skills`. In Claude Code, you can also install it as a plugin: ``` /plugin marketplace add crmne/ruby_llm /plugin install rubyllm@ruby_llm ``` See [AI Coding Assistants](https://rubyllm.com/ai-coding-assistants/) for setup and updates. ## Documentation [Guides](https://rubyllm.com/getting-started/) · [API reference](https://rubyllm.com/api/) · [Models](https://rubyllm.com/available-models/) · [Upgrading](https://rubyllm.com/upgrading/) · [1.x docs](https://rubyllm.com/v1/) ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License Released under the MIT License.
